Only $bw,dw$ are possible edges between the attachments.
Three tests have three bridges adjacent to all of $X$.
By Lemma~\ref{core:assembly-general}(ii), the remaining test $B+ac+bd$ is planar precisely when $H_1+bd+cw$ is planar.
This completion is a $K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$, using $brd$ and $cp'w$, and is nonplanar. Its base $H_1+cw$ is planar.

Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H_1+bd+cw$, which must use $bd$.
Apply Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} with attachments $b,c,d,w$, added edges $bd,cw$, and original edges $bw,dw$ permitted on the subdivision.
Its pieces may belong to different components of $H_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$.
Each such component is adjacent to $w$ and at least one of $b,d$.
By Lemma~\ref{r2:retained-components}, at most one further component is needed to retain a $b$--$d$ path avoiding $c,w$, and at most one to retain a neighbor of $c$.
Contract each further component to a single vertex, and retain a minimal set of attaching edges satisfying \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}.
The fourth test still contains the subdivision, and the other three tests still fail. These connectivity conditions also keep the interior of $B$ connected and all four attachments present. Minimality therefore forces equality with a reduced graph.

The enumeration~\supp{E17} considers every partition of the retained subdivision pieces into interior components, every minimal choice of edges joining each component, and at most two further singleton components with the required attachments.
